name: Mark Wang
current_role: Founder, chairman and CEO/president, WinWay Technology (TWSE: 6515), Kaohsiung
profile: Mark Wang (Wang Chia-huang / 王嘉煌) founded WinWay Technology in 2001 after ~10 years at ASE's test unit Fulgent Electronics. WinWay makes IC test sockets and interfaces (now also MEMS probe cards) for clients incl. ASE, Nvidia and AMD; listed on TWSE in 2021, its shares surged with AI demand in 2026 and it is building a new plant in Renwu, Kaohsiung.
interesting_fact: WinWay started as a one-man company in Wang's Kaohsiung home with NT$2 million; it is now one of the world's top-five high-end logic IC test socket makers with ~1,200 staff, and its share price passed NT$10,000 in April 2026.
deep_cut_fact: A Chung Yuan University mechanical-engineering grad (not an EE), Wang says the test socket used when Motorola brought its first BGA-packaged chip to Fulgent was his invention. WinWay's break came in 2002 when ATI asked it to build 10 sockets in one week after a foreign supplier failed; he delivered on time.
notes: Romanized variously as Chia-Huang / Jiahuang Wang. The input's SEC insider link to Hilton Grand Vacations is a different Mark Wang (HGV CEO), not this person. Gives interviews to Taiwanese financial media (Mirror Media, Business Today, UDN).

name: Michael Mente
current_role: Co-founder, co-CEO and director, Revolve Group (NYSE: RVLV)
profile: Michael Mente co-founded Revolve with Mike Karanikolas in 2003 using about $50,000 of their savings; the LA-area online fashion retailer pioneered influencer marketing and went public in 2019. As co-CEO he oversees merchandising, brand and the customer experience, including owned brands and the Revolve Festival events.
interesting_fact: Neither founder had a fashion background — both came from a software startup (NextStrat). Mente: 'We don't have fashion backgrounds—we were in tech.' They were named 2015 EY Entrepreneurs of the Year (retail).
deep_cut_fact: Mente left USC's business program in 2000, a year early, to join enterprise-software firm NextStrat, where he met future co-founder Mike Karanikolas.
notes: IR contact listed in Revolve press releases (SVP IR Erik Randerson). Media contact in older releases was the agency Walker Drawas; not re-verified for 2026.

name: Chen Yin
current_role: Founder, chairman and general manager, Greenworks (Jiangsu) Co. (SZSE: 301260)
profile: Chen Yin founded Greenworks (Globe Tools) in Changzhou in 2002; it makes battery-powered lawn, garden and DIY tools sold under Greenworks and other brands, with factories in China, the U.S. and Vietnam. It listed on Shenzhen's ChiNext in February 2023; Chen controls a majority stake and still runs the company as chairman and GM.
interesting_fact: Chen is an outspoken advocate of replacing gas-powered outdoor equipment with batteries, arguing operators spend about $4 on electricity for every $100 they would spend on fuel; Greenworks launched its first lithium-ion string trimmer in 2007.
deep_cut_fact: Chen was named EY Entrepreneur of the Year 2016 China in the industrial products category. He studied engineering at Donghua University (formerly China Textile University) and earned an MBA at Warwick.
notes: IR email is from the 2024 interim report; the board secretary is now Li Yirui (per May 2026 earnings-call record). Chen gives occasional English-language trade-press interviews, so US Greenworks PR is a possible route.

name: Kelly Lee
current_role: Chairman (since Dec 2020) and CEO (since Mar 2021), Lungyen Life Service Corp. (TPEx: 5530), Taiwan
profile: Kelly Lee (李凱莉) is the elder daughter of Lee Shih-tsung, founder of Lungyen, Taiwan's leading funeral, cemetery and columbarium services group. She succeeded him as chairman in December 2020 and as CEO in 2021, becoming the largest individual shareholder, and now runs the listed company's funeral services, columbaria and pre-need contract businesses.
interesting_fact: Lungyen is one of the few publicly listed 'death care' companies in Asia; Lee took the chair in a planned succession in December 2020 and spent her first month meeting every department head to learn the business.
notes: Very low public profile; no personal interviews found. Taiwanese coverage of the succession dwells on family matters — avoid. Investor relations page: https://www.lyls.com.tw/sitepage/investorrelations (no email published).

name: Jiang Chun
current_role: Chairman, Anhui Truchum Advanced Materials & Technology (Chujiang New Materials, SZSE: 002171), Wuhu
profile: Jiang Chun (姜纯), born 1960 in Wuhu, has spent 40+ years in copper processing. He built Truchum (楚江新材) into a major maker of copper strip, wire and specialty alloys, later expanding into carbon-fiber composites and high-end equipment via acquisitions; he is the controlling shareholder and chairman.
interesting_fact: Jiang has used acquisitions as Truchum's main growth engine, steering a traditional copper-processing business into advanced materials such as carbon-fiber composites for aerospace.
deep_cut_fact: A metal-forming (压力加工) graduate of Jiangxi Institute of Metallurgy, Jiang joined the newly founded Wuhu Nonferrous Metal Rolling Mill in 1986 and became its director in 1991 at age 31, turning the near-bankrupt plant profitable.
notes: Board-office email listed in the 2024 annual report. Rarely gives interviews; Chinese-language outreach advisable.

name: John Kirkland
profile: John Kirkland OBE, former chairman of the Derbyshire builder Bowmer & Kirkland (founded 1923 by his grandfather Robert Kirkland and Alfred Bowmer), died in November 2021 aged 83. The family's fortune continues to be listed in the Sunday Times Rich List as 'the Kirkland family'.
notes: Deceased (Nov 2021) per Construction Enquirer: https://constructionenquirer.com/2021/11/15/former-bommer-kirkland-chairman-dies . Bowmer & Kirkland remains family-owned; any outreach would be to the next generation via the company.

name: Shantaben Karsanbhai Patel
current_role: Member of the Nirma Group founding family (wife of founder Karsanbhai Patel, per her name); no active executive role found
profile: Shantaben Patel appears on rich lists via a stake in the Nirma Group, the Ahmedabad conglomerate (detergents, soaps, cement, soda ash, pharma) founded in 1969 by Karsanbhai Patel. Nirma began as a one-man after-office business selling cheap detergent door-to-door and became a national brand that undercut multinationals.
interesting_fact: Nirma started in 1969 with Karsanbhai Patel making detergent in his backyard and cycling through Ahmedabad neighbourhoods selling it at Rs 3/kg, about one-third the price of leading brands.
notes: Very private; no public profile or interviews found. Her role and relation are inferred from the listing name, not confirmed by a source. Company general address only. The web-search budget ran out for this item, so verification is limited.

name: Sagar Chordia
current_role: Listed with Panchshil Realty (Pune); exact title unverified (Panchshil's site names Atul Chordia as chairman)
profile: Sagar Chordia is listed as a source of wealth tied to Panchshil Realty, the Pune luxury and commercial developer founded in 2002 by Atul Chordia. Its projects include the EON Free Zone and World Trade Center Pune, Trump Towers Pune and yoopune (with Philippe Starck). Its hospitality arm Ventive Hospitality (a JV with Blackstone) listed in India in December 2024.
interesting_fact: Panchshil's 2010 yoopune residences were designed with Philippe Starck and John Hitchcox's YOO group, and the firm brought Marriott's Courtyard brand to Pune the same year.
notes: Could not confirm his title from a source after the web-search budget ran out. Commonly reported as Atul Chordia's son and a Panchshil director; verify before outreach. The IR email is for affiliate Ventive Hospitality.
